theater: 巴伐利亞與摩拉維亞戰線

battle.name: 法瑞戰爭
battle.theater: 巴伐利亞與摩拉維亞戰線
battle.brief: 一八〇五年，第三次反法同盟成形，法軍在巴伐利亞與摩拉維亞兩線壓向俄奧聯軍：烏爾姆開城、布拉格方向失誤、奧斯特里茨一役定局。野砲是這場戰爭的骨幹火力，六門一組的砲兵連，四磅與八磅野砲各拉六匹馬，隨軍團推著走，讓法軍第一次能把砲火當算式一樣帶進戰場。

kit.name: 野砲
kit.history: 能拆成幾件馬車拉走的砲。它讓野戰第一次有了可以計算的砲火。

countries: 一八〇五年的法瑞戰爭，實質是拿破崙的法蘭西帝國對抗第三次反法同盟，兩邊都是成體系的政府軍與盟軍聯隊。進攻方以拿破崙一世為最高統帥，法軍以軍團為作戰單位：每個步兵師自帶一個六門砲兵連，騎兵師配屬砲兵連，另設直屬大軍的預備砲兵營，由加桑迪中將統籌調度，軍需則由達魯總監以縱隊車隊供應。法軍陣內還有同盟國的部隊：西班牙王國出兵最多，北方由拉羅馬納侯爵率西班牙軍團進入巴伐利亞配合法軍，東面由蘇萊在巴倫西亞指揮法西聯軍；巴達維亞共和國、拿破崙兼領的義大利王國，以及被迫配合的那不勒斯王國也各派兵馬。防守方以俄羅斯帝國、奧地利帝國與大不列顛王國為骨幹：俄國由沙皇亞歷山大一世親裁軍政，兵分兩路，古圖佐夫在加利西亞邊境以拖延戰術拖住法軍先頭，本尼格森率主力南下；奧地利由弗朗茨皇帝與總參謀長麥克元帥節制，兵力重壓烏爾姆，多瑙河防線拉得過長；英國由小皮特主持國策，皇家海軍由納爾遜在海面施壓，並拉攏瑞典、那不勒斯、葡萄牙與兩西西里加入。普魯士、鄂圖曼與美國保持中立，卻在外交、糧價與走私上左右戰局。
countriesEn: The war of 1805 between France and Russia was, in substance, Napoleon's French Empire set against the Third Coalition, and both sides fielded fully organised regular armies together with contingents from allied and satellite states. On the attacking side Napoleon I was the supreme commander and the French fought as army corps: every infantry division carried its own six-gun foot battery, cavalry divisions had horse batteries attached, and a reserve artillery park belonging directly to the grand army was placed under the orders of General Gassendi, while the commissariat under the director Daru fed the columns through an endless wagon train. The French coalition of 1805 also contained troops of allied states: the Kingdom of Spain contributed the most, the Marquis de la Romana leading a Spanish corps into Bavaria in the north to operate with the French, while Suchet commanded a Franco-Spanish force in the Valencia area in the east; the Batavian Republic, the Kingdom of Italy over which Napoleon personally reigned, and the Kingdom of Naples, forced into line for the time being, all supplied men. On the defensive side the backbone was Russia, Austria and Great Britain. Alexander I governed Russia in person, dividing the army into two groups, with Kutuzov delaying the leading French columns on the Galician frontier while Bennigsen brought the main body south. Austria was directed by Emperor Francis and his chief of staff Mack, the bulk of the troops pressed onto Ulm behind a Danube line far too long for the men available. Britain was guided by the younger Pitt, the Royal Navy under Nelson pressed the enemy at sea, and Sweden, Naples, Portugal and the Two Sicilies were drawn into the alliance. Prussia, the Ottoman Empire and the United States remained neutral, yet their diplomacy, grain prices and quietly permitted smuggling shaped the result.
people: 拿破崙一世是這場戰爭的絕對主角，他自任大軍統帥，渡萊茵、圍烏爾姆、戰奧斯特里茨三個關鍵動作都出自我方。俄方由古圖佐夫與本尼格森先後統兵，兩人皆主張避免會戰、拖延對手，最後仍被迫在奧斯特里茨被合圍；巴格拉季昂的縱隊獨擋法軍右翼，表現最為突出，卻因奧軍不配合而覆沒。奧方由麥克元帥在烏爾姆獨當一面，基恩邁爾在布拉格方向倉促應戰，利希滕斯坦因在列寧方向支撐殘局，都是敗局中的關鍵人物；奧地利大公約翰在高林登獨力迎戰莫羅，雖敗仍拖住奧軍後路。西班牙方面，拉羅馬納在北方帶兵，蘇萊在東線作戰，萊基率領的西班牙輔助軍團加入德國戰線，福伊師在奧斯特里茨損失慘重，瓦爾德卡比亞在卡塔利亞以西班牙野砲對抗英西西里軍。海上，納爾遜戰死於特拉法加，科貝諾接掌殘局，維爾納夫與迪佩雷率法西聯合艦隊；英國政界由小皮特頂住輿論壓力，普魯士的弗里德里希·威廉三世選擇袖手旁觀，瑞典王儲伯納多特加入同盟卻被別處戰事牽制。這場戰爭的走向，最後仍落在少數幾個關鍵決定上。
peopleEn: Napoleon I was the absolute protagonist of the war; as commander-in-chief of the grand army he took the three decisions that shaped the campaign himself, the crossing of the Rhine, the encirclement of Ulm and the battle of Austerlitz. On the Russian side Kutuzov and Bennigsen commanded in turn, and both argued for avoiding a general engagement and stretching the enemy in the hope of buying time, yet they were cornered and fought at Austerlitz all the same. Bagration's column held the French right wing with conspicuous gallantry and was destroyed because the Austrian advance never came up to support it. The Austrians were led by Mack alone at Ulm, by Kienmayer in the hurried defence of the Prague road and by Liechtenstein on the Leitha side, all of them decisive figures in a lost cause; the archduke John met Moreau alone at Hohenlinden and, though beaten, still held up the Austrian rear. On the Spanish side La Romana led the northern army, Suchet fought in the east, Lecchi's Spanish auxiliary corps entered the German theatre, Foy's division was mauled at Austerlitz, and Valdecabia faced the Anglo-Sicilian force at Castalla with Spanish field guns. At sea Nelson was killed at Trafalgar and Codrington inherited the wreckage, while Villeneuve and Duperré led the combined French and Spanish fleet; in London Pitt bore the political strain of the war, Frederick William III of Prussia chose to stand aside, and Sweden's crown prince Bernadotte entered the coalition but was drawn away by fighting elsewhere. The direction of the war came down, in the end, to a handful of decisions taken by a handful of men.
kits: 野砲這件兵器在戰爭裡的位置，要從它的血統講起。野砲之所以成野砲，靠的是一五五〇年代之後定型的兩段式炮架：炮身坐在炮架上，前面用前車承載彈藥、工具與備件，套上六匹馬就能行軍，卸下馬匹即可射擊。整場戰爭的火力骨幹，就是把這種砲沿標準化路徑大量複製：一七七二年起推行的格里博瓦爾制式把野砲定為四磅與八磅兩種口徑，一門砲連前車共需六匹馬，八磅砲需八匹，一個六門的步兵砲兵連由四門六磅或八磅砲加兩門四磅砲組成，另配臼砲。一八〇五年德國戰役中，每個步兵師自帶一個這樣的砲兵連，砲跟著師走；真正決定會戰的火力則集中在直屬大軍的預備砲兵營，奧斯特里茨一役法軍在戰場上擺出的野砲約一百四十門，遠超此前任何會戰。西班牙砲兵同樣大量使用野砲，但保留較多的舊式義大利與丹麥制式，與新式混編，卡塔利亞的兩度交鋒裡，西班牙野砲陣地與英軍野砲的射界競逐是戰局關鍵。步槍方面，法軍用沙爾萊維爾前裝滑膛槍，英軍用一七九五年式燧發槍，奧軍用一七七七年式燧發槍，野砲射程之外的一切仍由刺刀與齊射決定。砲兵之外，軍隊還攜帶浮橋、攻城臼砲與龐大的攻城砲隊，炮手、馬匹、彈藥與隨營車隊是野砲能開火的前提，缺一不可。兩個插曲值得記下：法軍帶了一支小隊火箭兵到奧斯特里茨，火箭射程雖遠，精度卻不足以取代野砲；海戰方面，英軍速射船上的卡戎砲與西班牙沿岸的海岸砲台，是這場戰爭裡海權與陸權兩套砲術的交會點。奧斯特里茨之後，拿破崙把預備砲兵營集中使用的辦法抄成準則，野砲從此成為歐洲陸軍的標準配備。與此同時，英國對歐洲海岸的封鎖切斷了法國硝石與火藥的來源，一八〇六年之後法軍野外射擊的份量明顯受限，這是這場戰爭留下的硬傷之一。
kitsEn: The place of the field gun in this war can only be understood from its pedigree. What made a field gun a field gun was the two-part carriage that took shape after the middle of the sixteenth century: the gun sat on a trail, a limber carried the ammunition, tools and spare parts in front, six horses pulled the whole assembly on the march, and the team was simply unhitched for firing. The backbone of the firepower in this campaign was the mass reproduction of that idea along a standardised path. The Gribeauval system, worked out from 1772 and formally adopted in 1792, fixed the field piece at two calibres, four and eight pounds; a gun with its limber needed six horses and an eight-pounder eight; an infantry battery of six guns was made up of four six- or eight-pounders and two four-pounders, with howitzers. During the German campaign of 1805 each infantry division marched with just such a battery, the guns following the division; the firepower that actually decided the battle was massed in the reserve artillery park of the grand army, and at Austerlitz the French fielded on the field of some one hundred and forty guns, more than in any previous engagement. The Spanish artillery used field guns in great numbers as well, but retained more of the older Italian and Danish patterns mixed with the new, and at the two battles of Castalla the duel between the Spanish gun line on the ridge and the British field guns decided the rhythm of the fighting. Beyond the guns, muskets did the close work: the Charleville musket in French service, the 1795 pattern flintlock in British, the 1777 pattern in Austrian, with everything beyond the reach of the field gun settled by bayonet and volley. The artillery travelled with pontoons, siege howitzers and the heavy siege train, and gunners, horses, ammunition and baggage wagons were the precondition of every shot. Two side episodes deserve mention: a small troop of French rocket artillery brought rockets to Austerlitz, and although their range was long their accuracy never came close to replacing the field gun; at sea, the carronades carried by British fast-sailing craft and the coastal batteries of the Spanish shore marked the meeting point of two different artillery traditions. After Austerlitz Napoleon wrote the massing of the reserve park down as doctrine, and the field gun became standard equipment in every European army. At the same time the British blockade cut French imports of saltpetre and gunpowder, and the ammunition restrictions that followed from 1806 visibly blunted French shooting power in the field, one of the hard limits left behind by the war.
tactics: 法軍的戰術骨架是軍團分散、砲火集中。步兵師攜帶自己的六門砲兵連前進，縱隊行軍時砲在隊尾，展開成師時砲連佔據射界，步兵以密集縱隊前進，抵近後才展開成師方陣衝鋒；真正吃重的火力由加桑迪率領的大軍預備砲兵營集中使用，在決定性時刻一次投入，形成密集的野砲群。奧斯特里茨的部署最能說明這一點：拿破崙主動讓出普拉岑高地與其間的縱隊通道，引誘聯軍中央突入，卻把法軍縱隊分置左右兩翼，由達武的第三軍團在桑通山一線頂住聯軍右翼攻勢，由勒菲弗與莫蒂埃在更南的索爾科尼茨方向遮斷敵軍退路；普拉岑被聯軍奪得後才發現左右兩翼法軍同時壓上，高地上一部分聯軍砲兵因射角受限而無法有效支援，砲火反成累贅。俄軍縱隊在布拉格方向的推進，以及聯軍在高地上的砲兵居高射擊，構成了整場會戰的另一面。騎兵由穆拉特率領，在普拉岑與薩茨漢之間反衝失利，被法軍預備騎兵收拾，戰局仍回到步兵與野砲。烏爾姆之戰是另一種示範：麥克把奧軍沿多瑙河縱深配置，法軍卻以多瑙河上游的強渡作迂迴，切斷防線各段，迫使分遣的奧軍各個被殲。海上採縱陣戰鬥，納爾遜令戰列縱隊依次插入敵縱陣，砲火集中在接舷瞬間齊射，縱陣的航速加上火砲射程，使法西聯合艦隊在橫陳的縱列前無法展開。西班牙戰線的卡塔利亞是典型的小兵力野戰：英西西里軍以縱隊急行穿插，法西聯軍把野砲壓在山脊線後，砲口視界決定攻守節奏，十二月的第三次交鋒，英軍奪回卡塔利亞。整體而言，這是一場拒絕持久戰、逼對手速戰速決的戰爭：法軍靠集中砲火與快速機動，迫使對手在不利地形上決戰，聯軍則因指揮分散、步砲協同不足而步步退讓。冬季補給的緊張更把速決推成唯一選項，法軍在十一月的巴伐利亞幾乎斷糧。
tacticsEn: The tactical skeleton of the French army was dispersion in manoeuvre and concentration of fire. An infantry division carried its own six-gun battery, the guns trailing at the rear of the column on the march; when the division deployed, the battery took up its arc of fire, the infantry advanced in dense columns, and only at close range did it deploy into battalion squares for the final rush. The weight of the fire came from the reserve artillery park led by Gassendi, thrown into action at the decisive moment to form a dense mass of field guns. The deployment at Austerlitz illustrates the method best: Napoleon deliberately gave up Pratzen Heights and the defile between them, luring the Allied centre forward while placing his columns on both flanks, Davout's third corps holding the Santon heights against the Allied right, and Lefebvre and Mortier further south at the Telnitz and Sokolnitz covering the retreat route. Only when the Allies had seized Pratzen did they find the French closing in on both sides, and part of the Allied artillery on the heights, its arc restricted, could not support the attack and became a burden instead. The Russian advance along the Prague road and the Allied guns firing down from the heights form the other half of the battle. Murat's cavalry counter-charged between Pratzen and the Satschan and was broken, the reserve horse finishing the business, and the issue still came back to infantry and field guns. Ulm was the opposite lesson: Mack deployed the Austrians in depth along the Danube while the French forced a crossing further upstream, cut the line into separate sections and defeated each in turn. At sea the war was fought in line of battle, Nelson bringing his ships in one by one to pierce the enemy line, the guns concentrating on a single broadside at the moment of contact, so that the combined fleet drawn up in a long line could never bring its weight to bear. Castalla in Spain was a small battle in the open: the Anglo-Sicilian column hurried through the passes while the Franco-Spanish army kept its field guns behind a ridge line, the gun sight deciding the rhythm of attack and defence, and in December the British took the hill back. In general this was a war that refused attritional siege and forced the opponent into a quick decision. The French concentrated their guns and used mobility to bring the enemy to battle on ground of their own choosing, while the Allies gave ground step by step because their command was dispersed and their foot and horse batteries did not work together. The strain of winter supply made the quick decision the only option, the French being close to starving in Bavaria in November.
data: 這場戰爭留下來的數字不少，但史家對同一場戰役的損失常有出入，只能取其概略。兵力方面，一八〇五年渡過萊茵的法軍被記為約十八萬至二十萬人，其中真正投入德國戰役的軍團與西班牙輔助軍團合計約十二萬人上下；奧地利軍在烏爾姆一線約七萬五千至八萬人，多瑙河防線綿延近百公里；俄軍波羅的海與波蘭兩支部隊合計約六萬至八萬人。奧斯特里茨一役，法軍與盟軍合計約十四萬至十五萬人出戰，砲兵方面法軍在場野砲約一百四十門，聯軍約九十門，這是當時任何會戰未曾有過的砲兵密度。損失方面，烏爾姆之戰奧軍被俘約二萬七千人；奧斯特里茨法軍陣亡約一千二百人、受傷約七千人、被俘約三千人，聯軍陣亡約四千人、受傷約一萬五千人、被俘約七千人。海上，特拉法加海戰英軍陣亡四百四十九人、受傷約一千零四十人，法西聯合艦隊陣亡約三千四百人，傷者與溺斃者合計逾八千人，被俘七千至八千人，二十一艘法西主力艦與艦隊中相當一部分商船被英軍繳獲。野砲本身的數據相對明確：四磅砲有效射程約四百至五百步，八磅砲約五百至六百步，最大射程約五千至六千公尺；一個六門砲兵連連同乘員約八十至一百人，配馬十二至十四匹；每發四磅與八磅的裝藥量分別為一磅與八磅，另有群彈供近距離使用。這些數字多來自參戰者的回憶與各國參謀部的戰報，彼此對不上之處不少，但足以說明一八〇五年的會戰已經是大規模的砲兵對決，而不是十八世紀式的密集縱隊對射。
dataEn: The war left a good number of figures, but historians differ over the losses of the same battle, so only a rough picture is possible. On strength, the French army that crossed the Rhine in 1805 is usually given as about one hundred and eighty to two hundred thousand men, of whom perhaps one hundred and twenty thousand were actually committed to the German theatre, Spanish auxiliary corps included; the Austrian army on the Ulm front numbered roughly seventy-five to eighty thousand men behind a Danube line close to a hundred kilometres long; the Russian Baltic and Polish formations together came to some sixty to eighty thousand. At Austerlitz the French and their allies fielded around one hundred and forty to one hundred and fifty thousand men, and on the gun side about one hundred and forty field pieces stood on the French ground against about ninety for the Allies, a density of artillery never seen in any earlier battle. In losses, some twenty-seven thousand Austrians were taken prisoner at Ulm; at Austerlitz the French counted roughly one thousand two hundred killed, some seven thousand wounded and about three thousand prisoners, while the Allies lost about four thousand killed, some fifteen thousand wounded and around seven thousand captured. At sea, Trafalgar cost the British 449 dead and about 1,040 wounded; the combined French and Spanish fleet lost about 3,400 dead, more than eight thousand wounded or drowned, and between seven and eight thousand prisoners, while twenty-one French and Spanish ships of the line and a large part of the merchant fleet fell to the British. The gun figures are more firmly fixed: the four-pounder had an effective range of roughly four to five hundred paces, the eight-pounder five to six hundred, with a maximum range of some five to six thousand metres; a six-gun battery required about eighty to a hundred men all told and twelve to fourteen horses; each four-pounder and eight-pounder round carried one pound and eight pounds of shot respectively, with canister for close range. These numbers come mostly from the recollections of participants and the reports of the various staffs, and they do not always agree with each other, but they are enough to show that a battle of 1805 was already a massed duel of artillery rather than the dense column fire of the eighteenth century.
cause: 打起上來的緣由，一半是歐洲的政治格局，一半是法國的擴張速度。拿破崙在二〇〇四年加冕為法蘭西人的皇帝，又兼任義大利王國之王，把教宗國的世俗權力收歸己有；對奧地利而言，法國在義大利北部與萊茵一帶的實際控制，等於把奧帝國的戰略門戶堵死。俄國沙皇亞歷山大一世在與拿破崙會談破裂後回到東正教聯盟的舊框架，願與英國結盟，並把目光投向波蘭與奧地利，替奧地利壯膽。英國自一七九三年起與法國交戰，一八〇五年四月趁法軍在歐洲大陸作戰而再度宣戰，並拉上瑞典、那不勒斯與葡萄牙，切斷法國與歐洲內地的貿易。直接點火的是幾件事：一八〇五年八月的聖伊爾德豐索條約破裂，俄國接受英國安排；九月法軍由貝納多特率軍團強渡萊茵，把武裝中立條約撕開，奧地利認定法國下一步就會吞掉德意志，於是倉促宣戰；十月拿破崙兼併那不勒斯王國，把一個波旁王室推上戰場，隨即引來英西西里聯軍在南義大利登陸。西班牙卻站在法國一方，因為查理四世與戈多伊相信法國會保障西班牙在美洲的帝國，而拿破崙需要西班牙的軍隊、錢袋與船隻。但他拒絕了普魯士要求補償的條件，於是普魯士保持中立，留到次年再與法國清算。技術上還有一層必然：法軍的軍團制與集中砲兵讓速決成為可能，而聯軍分散兵力、各自作戰的體制恰好相反，衝突因此難以避免。
causeEn: The reasons for the war were half European politics and half the speed of French expansion. Crowned emperor of the French in 1804 and king of Italy in his own right, Napoleon had also taken the temporal power of the Papacy into his own hands; for Austria, French control of northern Italy and the Rhine was a door slammed on the empire's strategic approaches. Alexander I of Russia, having broken off his talks with Napoleon, fell back into the old framework of the Holy Alliance, was willing to ally with Britain, and turned his eyes towards Poland and Austria, which heartened the Austrians. Britain had been at war with France since 1793 and declared again in April 1805, while the French armies were committed on the continent, drawing in Sweden, Naples and Portugal and cutting French trade with the interior of Europe. Several events lit the fuse directly: the Treaty of San Ildefonso of August 1805 fell apart and Russia accepted British arrangements; in September the French corps under Bernadotte crossed the Rhine, tearing up the armistice of armed neutrality, and Austria judged that the next French step would be the swallowing of Germany, so it declared war in haste; in October Napoleon annexed the Kingdom of Naples, putting a Bourbon family on the field and bringing the Anglo-Sicilian landing in southern Italy in its wake. Spain, by contrast, stood on the French side, because Charles IV and Godoy believed France would guarantee the Spanish empire in the Americas, while Napoleon needed Spanish troops, money and shipping. He refused, however, the compensation Prussia demanded, so Prussia stayed neutral and settled accounts with France a year later. There was a technical inevitability as well: the French corps system and their massed artillery made a quick decision possible, while the Allies dispersed their forces and fought separate battles, and the collision was therefore hard to avoid.
impact: 這場戰爭是拿破崙權力的頂點，同時是整個拿破崙時代的起點。陸上，第三次同盟崩潰，奧地利在布雷斯堡和約裡割出威尼斯王國、蒂羅爾、特倫托與的里雅斯特，軍隊被限制在四萬三千人，並付出三百萬法郎賠款，奧地利此後十年不再是決策者。這個結果讓法國得以在次年組成萊茵邦聯，把漢薩城市納入自己的秩序，直接導致一八〇六年對普魯士的戰爭與耶拿、奧爾施泰特的慘敗，歐洲再沒有能獨力制衡法國的國家。海上，特拉法加確立了英國數十年的制海權，皇家海軍得以封鎖歐洲海岸；法國的海外貿易與原料來源被切斷，財政赤字與物價同步惡化，一八〇六年的大陸封鎖令與隨後的西班牙戰事，幾乎都可以回溯到這一年的封鎖。西班牙是最耐人尋味的角色：它以同盟國身份出兵最多，事後卻被迫接受一八〇六年的巴黎條約，交出佛羅里達與聖多明各，並在托斯卡納與帕爾馬的調換中失去地中海的據點；英軍在卡塔利亞戰線的反覆得手，更暴露了西班牙軍隊的士氣與訓練問題，為一八〇八年的起義埋下伏筆。俄國在慘敗中確認奧地利不可靠，一八〇七年轉向提爾西特與法國結盟，歐洲進入以法國為中心的新秩序期。軍事技術上，這是砲兵第一次在大規模會戰裡壓過步兵與騎兵：集中使用的野砲群、統一的口徑與標準的六門砲兵連，確立了後來歐洲陸軍炮兵組織的基本樣板，一直影響到十九世紀中葉的普魯士改革。史家也提醒，這個頂點靠的是短期的戰爭紅利而非長期的經濟基礎，大陸體系的張力早在拿破崙自己眼中就已埋下隱憂。
impactEn: This war was the high point of Napoleonic power and the starting point of the whole Napoleonic era. On land the Third Coalition collapsed. Austria, by the Peace of Pressburg, ceded Venetia, the Tyrol, the Trentino and Trieste, was limited to an army of forty-three thousand men, and paid three million francs in indemnity; for the following ten years Austria was no longer a decision maker. The result allowed France to form the Confederation of the Rhine in the next year and to pull the Hanseatic cities into its own order, which led directly to the war with Prussia in 1806 and the crushing defeats at Jena and Auerstedt; after that no European state could balance France on its own. At sea Trafalgar established British command of the sea for decades and the Royal Navy was able to blockade the European coasts; French overseas trade and raw material supplies were cut off, the deficit and prices deteriorated together, and the Continental System of 1806 together with the Spanish war that followed can largely be traced back to that blockade. Spain is the most instructive case: it supplied the largest allied contingent and afterwards had to accept the Treaty of Paris of 1806, giving up Florida and Santo Domingo and losing Mediterranean outposts in the exchange of Tuscany for Parma; the repeated British success on the Castalian front exposed the morale and training faults of the Spanish army and helped prepare the ground for the rising of 1808. Russia, after its defeat, concluded that Austria was unreliable and turned to alliance with France at Tilsit in 1807, so that Europe entered a period of French-centred new order. Technologically this was the first time artillery overrode infantry and cavalry on a large battlefield: massed field guns, unified calibres and standardised six-gun batteries established the basic pattern of artillery organisation in European armies for the next half century, right up to the Prussian reforms of the mid nineteenth century. Historians also warn that the summit rested on short-term war profits rather than a durable economic base, and that the strain inside the continental system was already visible to Napoleon himself.
result: 戰局以法軍的全面勝利收場，但勝利並不等於戰爭結束。陸路上，十月二十日奧地利軍在烏爾姆開城，麥克率殘部退往維也納，二十餘日內約二萬七千人淪為俘虜；同日法軍越過萊茵，把拿破崙的作戰重心推向巴伐利亞。二十一日，特拉法加海戰在加的斯外海爆發，納爾遜陣亡，法西聯合艦隊主力盡失，海上主權易手。十一月至十二月，拿破崙的軍隊拿下列寧、蒂羅爾與布魯克諾，聯軍在布拉格與列寧之間的協調失敗，莫羅在高林登再勝一仗，把奧軍從巴伐利亞逐向內陸。十二月二日，奧斯特里茨之役以法軍大勝收場，聯軍陣亡、被俘與丟棄的砲車數以萬計，亞歷山大一世與弗朗茨皇帝先後離開戰場；十二月二十六日簽訂布雷斯堡和約，十日之後法國取得威尼斯、蒂羅爾與特倫托的正式割讓。西班牙戰線上，七月二十一日的卡塔利亞由法西聯軍取勝，十二月十日的第三次交鋒則被英西西里軍奪回，但那不勒斯方面，英軍自十一月登陸後圍困加埃塔，要到一八〇六年一月二十六日守軍才開城投降。整體結果是：第三次同盟瓦解，法國取得德意志與義大利北部的直接控制，海洋歸英國，海峽與沿岸要塞歸法西聯軍。法國的勝利因此建立了長達十年的歐洲霸權，但同一場勝利也把歐洲推向更大的衝突，普魯士在次年加入反法陣線，俄國與瑞典也各自被迫應戰，制度性的對抗才剛剛開始。
resultEn: The campaign ended in a sweeping French victory, though victory did not mean the war was over. On land the Austrian army capitulated at Ulm on 20 October, Mack leading the survivors back towards Vienna and some twenty-seven thousand men falling into captivity within a fortnight; the same day the French crossed the Rhine and shifted the weight of Napoleon's operations into Bavaria. On 21 October the battle of Trafalgar was fought off Cadiz, Nelson was killed and the main body of the combined fleet was lost, transferring command of the sea. From November into December the French took Leiningen, the Tyrol and Bregenz, the Allies lost their chance to coordinate between Prague and the Leitha, and Moreau won again at Hohenlinden, driving the Austrians out of Bavaria into the interior. On 2 December the battle of Austerlitz ended in a decisive French victory, the Allies losing tens of thousands dead, wounded and captured together with their guns and wagons, Alexander I and Emperor Francis leaving the field in turn; the Peace of Pressburg followed on 26 December, and ten days later France took formal possession of Venetia, the Tyrol and the Trentino. On the Spanish front Castalla was won by the Franco-Spanish army on 21 July, and the third meeting in December was taken back by the Anglo-Sicilian force; in Naples the British landed in November, besieged Gaeta, and only on 26 January 1806 did the garrison capitulate. The overall result was the dissolution of the Third Coalition, direct French control of Germany and northern Italy, the sea in British hands, and the straits and coastal fortresses shared with the Franco-Spanish side. French victory thus established a European hegemony that lasted a decade, but the same victory pushed Europe towards far larger conflicts: Prussia entered the anti-French front the following year, Russia and Sweden were drawn into new wars in their turn, and the institutional confrontation had barely begun before the greater wars of the Napoleonic period, culminating in 1812.
